attribution.note: Co-written essay on Marcus's Substack; 'Our view' is endorsed by the subject.

semantics.note: Firm 'will not work well until' is kept. The 'until' clause works as a necessary condition. The hedged 'may require wholesale revisions' part is kept as hedged and is not scorable.

contract.note: Neither 'work well' nor 'major progress in common sense' has a measure, and there is no deadline. The early-resolution rule is strict and fair. The looser support condition (agents keep failing) cannot settle an open-horizon forecast on its own.

evidence.note: 30% task completion by Sept 2025 shows agents still fall short. It does not address commonsense progress and does not meet either early-resolution rule.
Vendor's own statement that its agent is early-stage and error-prone. Company disclosure; it does not settle 'working well' or the cause.

reviews.rationale: Firm forecast with no deadline. No dated event meets the early-resolution rule: agents have not been shown to work reliably, and no commonsense breakthrough is documented as the cause. Continued shortfalls without a deadline do not settle it.

semantics.note: Unqualified 'will be' with a 2025 horizon. The proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: Plain reading (agents among the main themes of 2025 launches, research and analysis) is ordinary and fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: Operator launched Jan 2025. A company disclosure, but it documents a dated flagship agent launch.
ChatGPT agent launched July 2025 inside the flagship product. Company disclosure of a dated launch.
Independent index (published Feb 2026, before the cutoff) reports a substantial rise in attention to agents in 2025, including record paper counts.

reviews.rationale: The 2025 horizon has passed. Major labs launched flagship agent products during 2025, and an independent tracker reports a substantial rise in research and industry attention to agents that year. No counterevidence was found.

semantics.note: Firm causal claim: new failures keep appearing because there is no robust solution. Faithful to the statement.

contract.note: Readings of 'robust solution' and the late-2024 target period are supplied by the evaluator. Requiring intervention evidence for a causal claim is reasonable.

evidence.note: Documents spatial reasoning failures in 2024 models. Does not track fixes or show why failures persist.
Fine-tuned VLMs show some generalization in spatial reasoning. Cuts against the idea of pure patching, but shows no robust solution and does not test the causal claim.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows that failures continued and that some spatial generalization was possible. No study links fixes of individual examples to new failures, and none establishes or rules out the claimed cause. The evidence does not settle the causal claim.

semantics.note: A comparative historical observation through Jan 2025. The 'to date' scope is preserved.

contract.note: Reading 'much less effective' as a substantial gap in established practical breadth and reliability is ordinary and fair. No measure was given, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Disney film simulator shows simulation's value in entertainment. Only one side of the comparison.
NASA aircraft-design simulation shows engineering value. Only one side of the comparison.
An intuitive-physics simulation model generalizes on physical prediction. Mildly counter, but it models human cognition and shows no broad AI commonsense deployment.

reviews.rationale: The packet gives examples from only one side of each domain and no cross-domain comparison of effectiveness. It neither establishes nor refutes the 'much less effective' gap for AI commonsense reasoning.
